question: In which of the following years was Indian Universities Act enacted to impose stiff control over Indian Universities?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1904**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Universities Act** was enacted in **1904** under the viceroyalty of Lord Curzon to regulate and control the activities of universities in India.
 
• The act aimed to impose stricter control over universities and introduced reforms to improve the quality of higher education in India.
 
• The act increased government oversight in universities and introduced measures such as **more stringent regulations on affiliated colleges** and the appointment of university councils.
 
• It provided for the establishment of teaching universities such as the University of Punjab and reorganized the existing universities for better administration.
 
• The act also emphasized improving the standard of education, enhancing research facilities, and bringing uniformity in the functioning of universities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lord Curzon’s Educational Reforms:**

 
 
• Lord Curzon was the Viceroy of India from **1899 to 1905**, and he introduced significant reforms in education during his tenure.
 
• The Indian Universities Act of 1904 was part of his larger agenda to improve the quality of education in India and establish centralized control.
 
• He believed that the universities were becoming breeding grounds for political agitation, and stricter control was needed to curb these activities.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of the Indian Universities Act, 1904:**
 
 
• The act increased government control over universities, including the appointment of members to university councils by the government.
 
• Universities were required to seek government approval for their statutes, regulations, and ordinances.
 
• It introduced the provision for periodic inspection of universities by government officials.
 
• The act restricted the number of colleges that could be affiliated with a university to ensure better supervision and quality control.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Act:**
 
 
• The act faced criticism from Indian leaders and intellectuals as it was seen as an attempt to curtail academic freedom and impose colonial control over education.
 
• It led to resentment among Indian students and educators and contributed to the growing nationalist sentiment against British rule.
 
• Despite the opposition, the act did bring some structural improvements in the functioning of universities and laid the foundation for modern higher education in India.
 
 
 
• **Other Significant Education Reforms Under British Rule:**
 
 
• **Wood’s Despatch (1854):** Introduced the policy of promoting education in English and vernacular languages, focusing on higher education and teacher training.
 
• **Hunter Commission (1882):** Recommended measures to improve primary and secondary education and emphasized the need for female education.
 
• **Saddler Commission (1917-19):** Reviewed the state of university education in India and recommended reforms to make it more effective.
